PR.body:
Proposed plan issue **P0-48** (Gate G0, Urgent): make `build-test` finish on GitHub runners. It feeds P0-33 ("CI green on main"). Part of the [AMC Ready-to-Deploy Implementation Plan](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/153157e0-0d2f-4374-934b-5f6f360a46e1). Base: `main` @ `786d8abb`.

## Problem

Every `build-test` run from 2026-09-16 to 2026-10-05 was **cancelled at its job timeout, with no log uploaded**. That covers `main` and PRs #34, #36 and #37. The last green run was 2026-07-15. Runs ignored their own step timeouts, so the runner agent itself had stalled; no test reported a failure.

## Root cause

`tests/foreignSubagentRunner.test.ts`, test "a truncated answer is not an answer":
- Its fake agent prints 5 MiB with **no newline** (`head -c 5242880 /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'x'`).
- `spawnGovernedChild` tees child output to the parent's stdout.
- The resulting single 5,242,903-byte line in the Actions log stalls the runner.

Bisected on GitHub in probe #39 (now closed):

| Round | Run | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [37363461747](https://github.com/AgentMaturity/AgentMaturityCompass/actions/runs/37363461747) | Coverage or plain, default or 2 workers: all 4 died |
| 2 | [37371774017](https://github.com/AgentMaturity/AgentMaturityCompass/actions/runs/37371774017) | In a 12 GB container the runner still died; 87 GB disk and 13 GB RAM free |
| 3 | [37381278303](https://github.com/AgentMaturity/AgentMaturityCompass/actions/runs/37381278303) | 8 shards: only shard 8 hung |
| 4 | [37385666873](https://github.com/AgentMaturity/AgentMaturityCompass/actions/runs/37385666873) | Shard 8 in 8 parts: only part 4 hung |
| 5 | [37389641298](https://github.com/AgentMaturity/AgentMaturityCompass/actions/runs/37389641298) | 24 single-file jobs: only this file hung |
| 6 | [37392711874](https://github.com/AgentMaturity/AgentMaturityCompass/actions/runs/37392711874) | Original test, output to a file: runner survived. Patched test printing normally: passed in 1.5 min |

## Fix

1. In that one test, swallow the tee with `vi.spyOn(process.stdout, "write")`. The assertion is about what the runner records, not what it prints. Product behaviour is unchanged.
2. In `ci.yml` "Full suite and coverage thresholds" and `npm-publish.yml` "Test", pipe the runner-log copy through `cut -c1-4096`. The full output still goes to the log artifact through `tee`. Both steps use `shell: bash` (`-eo pipefail`), so the test exit status still fails the step. No future giant line can stall a runner.

Changeset: patch, "contributor tooling only, no runtime change".

## Proof

- **Regression evidence:** the probe rounds above. Locally, the original file writes one 5,242,903-byte line; with the fix its whole output is 420 bytes, and all 12 tests pass.
- **Mutation:** removing the spy brings the 5 MiB line back (round 6 shows what that does on GitHub).
- **Full local run of every CI step at `cde922e0`:**
  - 1,522 test files, 21,409/21,409 tests passed under coverage; per-file floors pass.
  - `release:gate` 17/19: only the D-11 source checks fail, as on `main`.
  - Related and parity tests: 34 files, 7,263 tests pass.
- **Acceptance:** this PR's own `build-test` jobs on GitHub must finish, for the first time since 2026-09-16.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Product question: the monitor tees a foreign child's output straight to the operator's stdout with no line or size bound. A real delegate that prints a huge single line would do the same thing to a user's CI runner when AMC runs inside GitHub Actions (for example through `amc-action`).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.messageBody:
The test's fake agent writes 5 MiB of output with no newline, and the
monitor tees child output to this process's stdout. That single 5 MiB
line reached the GitHub Actions log and stalled the runner until the
job timed out with no log uploaded: every build-test run from
2026-09-16 to 2026-10-05 was cancelled this way.

Found by bisecting the suite on GitHub (probe PR #39): 8 shards, then
8 parts of the hanging shard, then 24 single-file jobs. Only this file
killed its runner. With its output redirected to a file the runner
survived (exit 0, longest line 5,242,903 bytes); with this fix it
passes while printing normally (420 bytes in total locally).

The assertion is about what the runner records, so the tee is swallowed
with a spy on process.stdout.write for this one test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.messageBody:
The full test output still goes to the log artifact through tee. Only the
copy that reaches the Actions runner log is cut, so no future test that
prints a giant line can stall a runner again. pipefail keeps the test
command's exit status.

sourceEvidence.excerpt:
- name: Full suite and coverage thresholds
        timeout-minutes: 45
        shell: bash
        # The full output goes to the log artifact; the runner log gets lines cut at
        # 4,096 bytes. A test once teed a 5 MiB single-line answer to stdout, and a
        # line that long stalls the Actions runner until the job times out with no
        # log at all (every build-test run from 2026-09-16 to 2026-10-05).
        run: |
          mkdir -p tmp/ci-coverage
          npm run test:coverage -- --exclude 'tests/performance/**' --reporter=default --reporter=json --reporter=hanging-process --outputFile.json=tmp/ci-coverage/tests.json 2>&1 | tee tmp/ci-coverage/tests.log | cut -c1-4096

      # Throughput floors hold for uninstrumented code with the CPU to itself. Under
      # coverage, with every worker busy, the 500 ev/s control-plane floor measured
      # 477-496 ev/s on hosted runners, so the performance files run here instead.
      - name: Performance floors (no coverage, one file at a time)
        run: npx vitest run tests/performance --no-file-parallelism

      # Tests must use temp workspaces; a write to a tracked or untracked path
      # (for example .amc/keys/*) fails here. Ignored dist/, tmp/ and coverage/ do not show.
      - name: Tests left the checkout clean
        run: git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all > /tmp/after-tests.txt; if [ -s /tmp/after-tests.txt ]; then cat /tmp/after-tests.txt; exit 1; fi

      - name: Per-file coverage floors
        run: npm run check:coverage

      - name: Upload coverage diagnostics
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-diagnostics-node-${{ matrix.node-version }}
          path: |
            tmp/ci-coverage/
            coverage/coverage-summary.json
          if-no-files-found: ignore

# 4,096 bytes. A test once teed a 5 MiB single-line answer to stdout, and a
        # line that long stalls the Actions runner until the job times out with no
        # log at all (every build-test run from 2026-09-16 to 2026-10-05).
        run: |
          mkdir -p tmp/ci-tests
          npm test -- --reporter=default --reporter=json --reporter=hanging-process --outputFile.json=tmp/ci-tests/tests.json 2>&1 | tee tmp/ci-tests/tests.log | cut -c1-4096

      - name: Upload test diagnostics
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: npm-publish-test-diagnostics
          path: tmp/ci-tests/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Prepack release guardrails
        run: npm run release:prepack-check

  release:
    needs: test-build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:

dependenciesAndLimits: P0-48 feeds P0-33 CI qualification; assertion/coverage failures and matrix cancellation remain P0-33/inherited issue debt, separate from giant-line clipping.
Use Node22 and Node24 with pnpm10.33.0 and ABI-compatible installed dependencies in an owned isolated checkout. This preflight installed/rebuilt nothing.
GitHub job acceptance requires hosted execution evidence; local stdout capture is a scoped regression proof only.
No log cap is applied to the full diagnostic artifact: tee precedes cut. Explicit shell:bash actually logged bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail in current GitHub run.
Current npm-publish test step remains protected, but its release/publish behavior is outside P0-48 scope; do not trigger that workflow for a log qualification.
Raw foreign-child product stdout remains unbounded by this change, per explicit PR40 follow-up; no successor key is invented here.
